author: Jane Addams
title: Twenty Years at Hull-House, with Autobiographical Notes
edition: University of Pennsylvania 'A Celebration of Women Writers' transcription of New York: The Macmillan Company, 1912 printing (copyright 1910; first published November 1910), identified by its transcribed title, imprint and copyright leaves. Used in place of Project Gutenberg #1325, which derives from an earlier version of this transcription but alters dashes and several words. HTML tags, page numbers and illustration captions are omitted; a word divided across a page break is rejoined, and a compound hyphenated at a source line end (self-government, Hull-House) is closed up; a paragraph that the HTML splits around an illustration is rejoined; whitespace normalized. Chapter-opening small capitals appear as capitals, as transcribed. The library holds the Preface and Chapters I–XVIII with their numbers and titles as headings; the title page, contents, lists of plates and illustrations, and the site’s About This Edition note are omitted. The normalisations above are applied throughout the book: every word divided across a page break is rejoined (the three divided compounds Hull-House, half-crazed and junk-shops keep their hyphen), and every paragraph split around an illustration is rejoined.

rights.basis: Original English memoir first published in 1910 (Macmillan; magazine portions copyright 1910 Phillips Publishing); the 1912 printing used was also published before 1931, so its US term has expired as of 2026.

acquisition.method: UPenn A Celebration of Women Writers HTML. Kept the Preface and the chapters; removed comments, page-number, facing-page and verso markers, rules, every image with its centred caption paragraph, and the contents and illustration lists. Each P became a paragraph (whitespace collapsed, entities decoded, small-capital spans joined to their initials as transcribed); block-indented P elements (quoted verse) became stanzas with line-break tags as line ends and no-break-space indentation kept; each chapter H2 gave a level-2 number heading and a level-3 title heading. A word hyphenated before a page-number marker was joined without the hyphen, except three compounds (Hull-House twice, half-crazed, junk-shops); a hyphen at an HTML line end was closed up without a space. A paragraph resumed after an illustration (or in a P marked as a continuation) was joined to the previous paragraph when that one ended without closing punctuation or the resumed text began in lower case (41 places).
